correctness.rationale: Complete orthogonal decomposition of the unweighted one-hub clique-sum Laplacian produces three rational transition formulas. All positive denominators, positive spectral scalars, and a quartic with exactly one descending-coefficient sign change imply the precise nonreentrant positivity horizon. An independent direct matrix constructor checked 2,322 rational off-diagonal identities across 23 graphs, and exact rational sign substitutions isolate example roots; finite tests are supporting, not the all-parameter proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A method-wide theorem giving exact entrywise positivity for all nonnegative graph Laplacians would dominate the claim, but none of the inspected sources asserts one. Explicit RK4 R_4 and implicit Gauss [2/2] are different rational/polynomial maps; complete multipartite only contains the all-singleton star subfamily of these multi-petal clique sums, unless there is one petal (excluded by t>=2).

originality.rationale: An exact implication comparison with primary full-text SSP/Padé literature and published numerical-analysis records identifies no result settling these all-size nonstar clique-sum [2/2] Padé positivity thresholds; closest 2010 theorem gives sufficient positivity for Hurwitz Metzler systems, not our exact conservative family, and the graph spectral literature does not address timestep signs. This is a finite best-knowledge judgment with explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The publisher HTML for the 2026 windmill spectra paper displayed only abstract and bibliography; an application in its inaccessible full body was not ruled out.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies positivity for a natural heterogeneous hub-and-community graph family and a widely used fourth-order implicit method. It identifies a sharp graph-structural distinction (star-only unconditional positivity) and a nontrivial intermediate-petal earliest-failure effect, with an exact easily computed algebraic horizon. This is a substantive structural positivity classification, not a routine parameter substitution.
